messages:
marta: quick sync — i'm sketching a reclaim-agent that runs background compaction and slow slab merges. thinking we keep the evict-scheduler for latency-critical eviction decisions and let the reclaim-agent do low-priority repairs during idle windows. thoughts?
jeremy: you mean a separate process that can preemptively compact/poke free lists?
li: curious about the CPU and p99 impact — compaction can spike CPU and affect inference latency if not properly throttled.
sam: tenant fairness concern — background repairs shouldn't starve tenants or violate their reserved throughput. need admission controls.
perf-bot: recent telemetry: compaction jobs correlate with 99th latency spikes on some hosts (hostpool-7). details: https://telemetry.internal/hosts/hostpool-7/compaction-events :eyes:
marta: exact — reclaim-agent would be admission-controlled by load and tenant quotas. basic idea: only run when host_load < config.idle_threshold (default 0.55) and compaction_cpu_budget not exhausted. evict-scheduler stays in fast path for per-request decisions.
jeremy: what about race with eviction? e.g., reclaim moves pages, evict meanwhile tries to migrate. need handoff protocol.
li: agree. we should use the existing lease/token model: reclaim requests a soft-lease on slabs, evict-scheduler treats soft-lease as hint to avoid touching. if eviction needs the slab, it can preempt reclaim via lease-renegotiate and reclaim must yield.
sam: and we probably need a preemptible compaction loop — checkpoint frequently so reclaim can back off quickly.
marta: yep. pseudocode sketch:
```
while (true) {
  if (host.load() > idle_threshold) sleep(10s); continue;
  slab = choose_fragmented_slab();
  if (!acquire_soft_lease(slab)) continue;
  compact(slab, cpu_budget_ms=50); // preemptible
  release_soft_lease(slab);
}
```
li: love the preemptible slice idea. but we should avoid compacting very small slabs repeatedly — add hysteresis / cool-down per-slab.
jeremy: api boundary question: should reclaim-agent be part of runtime process or separate daemon? pros/cons?
marta: separate daemon easier to scale and crash-isolate, and can be rate-limited per-host. but cross-process lease interface needed — maybe unix socket or shared mmap for lease table.
li: shared mmap lease table seems low-latency and robust. plus it avoids auth plumbing.
sam: operational hooks: a Prometheus metric for reclaim.progress, reclaim.preemptions, slab.cooldowns. also an emergency-disable flag (feature-flag) for rollbacks.
marta: rollout plan: start on dev cluster with very conservative idle_threshold=0.3 and cpu_budget 20ms slices. canary to 5 hosts, monitor p99, error rates, compaction throughput.
jeremy: how to measure fragmentation benefit? we need delta in resident set or reduced eviction rate. propose metrics: avg_frag_score_per_slab, eviction_retries, pages_evicted_per_request pre/post.
li: add telemetry tag for tenant-id so we can detect if reclaim causes unfairness. also track reclaimed_pages_by_tenant.
marta: one more: integration with eviction backpressure — if eviction backlog grows, reclaim-agent should pause immediately. implement via simple backpressure counter exposed by evict-scheduler.
sam: do we need a global coordinator for multi-node compaction (to avoid thundering herd)? maybe a leader-elect per cluster pool.
marta: yes, leader per hostpool to avoid simultaneous heavy compactions across hosts that serve same tenants. but start simple: per-host only.
jeremy: will add these notes to the design doc. link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/reclaim-agent (WIP) :+1:
li: ok — i'll prototype the shared mmap lease table and a basic preemptible compactor loop.
perf-bot: FYI: hosts with lower avg_load show 2-3x better reclaim efficiency historically. dataset: last 90d.
marta: thanks — sync later today 3pm in #eng-runtime. :calendar:
